title.en: Effects of Physical Activities on Human Body
How your body upgrades when you move

text.en: When you sprint or play football, your heart beats faster, your lungs draw deeper breaths, and your muscles warm up. Over weeks of regular exercise, your organ systems actually grow stronger.

A healthy body depends on organ systems working in harmony—skeletal, muscular, respiratory, and circulatory systems.
Muscles are made of elongated muscle fibres. Voluntary muscles (limbs, neck) move by our will, while involuntary muscles line internal organs and cardiac muscle forms the heart.
Regular physical activity strengthens muscles, protects bones and joints from injury and arthritis, improves posture, and increases muscle oxygen use.
During exercise, respiratory rate rises and an 'oxygen debt' can occur when oxygen demand briefly exceeds intake; regular training increases vital capacity up to 5500 cc.
In the circulatory system, the right heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs via the pulmonary artery, and the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body via the aorta.
Long-term exercise strengthens the heart muscle, improves blood circulation, lowers bad cholesterol (LDL), and raises good cholesterol (HDL).
All organ systems work in unison whenever you walk, warm up, or play a sport.
Voluntary muscles move our limbs by choice; involuntary muscles work automatically inside organs.
Regular exercise builds muscle strength, protects joints, and prevents postural deformities.
During intense exercise, oxygen is used faster than intake, creating an oxygen debt.
Regular training expands vital capacity—the maximum air breathed in and out—up to 5500 cc.
Exercise lowers LDL (bad cholesterol) and increases HDL (good cholesterol), protecting the heart.

problem.en: Trace the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs to the body's organs.

text.en: Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium.

why.en: Pulmonary veins are the only veins carrying oxygenated blood.

text.en: Blood moves to the left ventricle and is pumped through the aorta to all body organs.

why.en: The aorta is the main artery leaving the left ventricle.

prompt.en: Explain what oxygen debt is and how regular exercise affects HDL and LDL cholesterol.

requiredIdeas.en: Oxygen debt occurs when intense exercise uses oxygen faster than it is taken in
Regular exercise raises vital capacity and strengthens the heart
Exercise increases HDL (good cholesterol) and decreases LDL (bad cholesterol)

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking arteries always carry oxygenated blood (the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs)

points.en: Voluntary, involuntary, and cardiac muscles coordinate movement and organ function.
Regular exercise strengthens muscles, protects joints, and corrects posture.
Respiratory vital capacity increases up to 5500 cc with regular physical activity.
Exercise improves heart efficiency, raises HDL (good cholesterol), and lowers LDL (bad cholesterol).
